notes: All values are Marlin's definitions at commit 2ef3ee6 as written in the six provided files; nothing here judges whether they match the physical board.

Agreement: the hand reading (manual_reading.py, written before any preprocessor run) matches the GCC -dD/-dM result for every macro in both configs on value, file and line (0 diffs), and clang -dM gives the same body for every board-chain macro.

How later files win here: the chain has no #undef. An unguarded #define of a macro that is already defined with a different body is a constraint violation that GCC/clang accept with a 'redefined' warning (not an error unless -Werror/-pedantic-errors), and the LATER definition takes effect. A guarded default (#ifndef X / #define X) later in the chain is skipped if an earlier file already defined X. So an earlier guard does not stop a later unguarded define from replacing it.

SURPRISE 1 - X_ENABLE_PIN: pins_FYSETC_SPIDER.h:68 defines PE9, then pins_FYSETC_S6.h:29 redefines it (unguarded) as PE12, so the effective X_ENABLE_PIN is PE12 in every config. PE12 is also TMC_SPI_SCK (pins_FYSETC_SPIDER.h:98).

SURPRISE 2 - TMC UART TX pins (config a only): pins_FYSETC_SPIDER.h:77-84 sets X/Y/Z/E0/E1/E2_SERIAL_TX_PIN = PE7/PE15/PD10/PD7/PC14/PC15, but pins_FYSETC_S6.h:35-46 (same #if HAS_TMC_UART, unguarded) redefines them as PE9/PE14/PD11/PD3/PC4/PE1 and adds *_SERIAL_RX_PIN = PE8/PE13/PD12/PA15/PC5/PE0. The S6 values win. Only X2_SERIAL_TX_PIN PA15 (SPIDER.h:78) and Z2_SERIAL_TX_PIN PD11 (SPIDER.h:81) come from the Spider file; X2/Z2 get no RX pin.

Fact for comparison: the overridden Spider TX values (PE7, PE15, PD10, PD7, PC14, PC15) equal X/Y/Z/E0/E1/E2_CS_PIN in pins_FYSETC_S6_common.h:84/89/94/99/104/109, and X2/Z2_SERIAL_TX_PIN equal X2/Z2_CS_PIN (SPIDER.h:50/55). The effective S6 TX/RX pins instead coincide with other macros in config (a): see same_pin_multiple_macros_a (e.g. PD12 = X2_STEP_PIN and Z_SERIAL_RX_PIN; PE1 = Z2_STEP_PIN and E2_SERIAL_TX_PIN; PE8 = X2_ENABLE_PIN and X_SERIAL_RX_PIN; PE14/PE13 = TMC_SPI_MOSI/MISO and Y_SERIAL_TX/RX_PIN).

SURPRISE 3 - BOARD_INFO_NAME: pins_FYSETC_SPIDER_V2_2.h:24 defines "FYSETC SPIDER V22", pins_FYSETC_SPIDER.h:25 is skipped by its #ifndef, then pins_FYSETC_S6.h:24 redefines it (unguarded) as "FYSETC S6", which wins. DEFAULT_MACHINE_NAME is BOARD_INFO_NAME (pins_FYSETC_SPIDER_V2_2.h:25), so it also expands to "FYSETC S6".

V2.2 / Spider values that win over S6 defaults (S6_common's #ifndef blocks are skipped): TEMP_BED_PIN PB0 (V2_2.h:29, not PC3 at S6_common:118), FAN0_PIN PA13 (V2_2.h:31, not PB0), FAN1_PIN PA14 (V2_2.h:32, not PB1), HEATER_0/1/2/BED = PB15/PC8/PB3/PB4 (SPIDER.h:60-63, not PB3/PB4/PB15/PC8), SERVO0_PIN PA2 (SPIDER.h:74, not PA3). FAN2_PIN PB2 (S6_common:143) is unguarded and comes from S6. TEMP_3_PIN PC3 and TEMP_4_PIN PB1 come only from V2_2.h:27-28.

Config dependency - TMC UART: every *_SERIAL_TX/RX_PIN is inside #if HAS_TMC_UART (SPIDER.h:76, S6.h:31) and is absent in config (b). The files test only HAS_TMC_UART, not X_DRIVER_TYPE etc. TMC_USE_SW_SPI and TMC_SPI_MOSI/MISO/SCK (SPIDER.h:90-99) are defined unconditionally in both configs; the SPI pins are #ifndef-guarded so a user Configuration could override them.

Config dependency - EEPROM (FLASH and LCD variants verified in extra_checks.txt): NO_EEPROM_SELECTED is a macro (pins.h:65) re-evaluated at each #if. With EEPROM_SETTINGS on and no type chosen, SPIDER.h:34-35 defines I2C_EEPROM; by S6_common.h:40 NO_EEPROM_SELECTED is now false, so S6_common.h:41 is skipped. MARLIN_EEPROM_SIZE 0x1000U is defined at SPIDER.h:41 and again identically at S6_common.h:50 (no warning). If FLASH_EEPROM_EMULATION is chosen, S6_common.h:48 defines FLASH_EEPROM_LEVELING instead and no MARLIN_EEPROM_SIZE comes from S6_common (the Spider #if ENABLED(I2C_EEPROM) at :40 is also false). With EEPROM_SETTINGS off (variant c), neither I2C_EEPROM nor MARLIN_EEPROM_SIZE is defined. No I2C bus pins or EEPROM address are defined in these files.

Config dependency - LCD: everything in pins_FYSETC_S6_common.h:194-280 depends on FYSETC_242_OLED_12864 / HAS_WIRED_LCD / CR10_STOCKDISPLAY / FYSETC_MINI_12864(_1_2/_2_0/_2_1) / FYSETC_GENERIC_12864_1_1 / IS_ULTIPANEL / REPRAP_DISCOUNT_FULL_GRAPHIC_SMART_CONTROLLER / IS_U8GLIB_ST7920 and is inactive in both configs (list in conditional_definitions_inactive_in_a).
